reviewMethod: Independent visual reading of all 20 question-paper pages and PDF pages 27–52 of the combined Higher Level scheme (the Paper 2 title page 27, the scale table on page 28 (misheaded “Paper 1”), the summary of mark allocations on page 29, every Paper 2 model solution and marking note on pages 30–47, the Irish-language bonus-marks page 48 and the blank back pages). Each task boundary is the published scale beside its model solution, cross-checked against the printed summary.
sourceNotes: The paper is 300 marks: candidates answer all nine questions (Section A Q1–6, 25 marks each; Section B Q7 55 marks, Q8 45 marks, Q9 50 marks). Every question is retained.
34 independently marked units, matching the printed summary of allocations on scheme page 29.

Paper 2 bands from the scale table on scheme page 28, which differ from Paper 1’s in the 10D ladder: 5B 0,2,5; 5C 0,2,4,5; 10B 0,5,10; 10C 0,3,7,10; 10D 0,3,5,8,10; 15C 0,5,10,15; 15D 0,4,7,11,15. Every part prints the same ladder beside its scale.

This paper had no authored cards before this review; all 34 units are new. Marking points are lifted line by line from the scheme (read through the glyph repair map) and labelled with the part of the scheme they come from; the scheme’s bullets are not reproduced. Stacked fractions are written a/b. Q3(b)’s mid partial credit prints 132·2° where its high partial credit prints 138·2°; both are quoted as printed.

Nine parts carry the SEC’s own print of their scheme row (model solution and every credit band), cropped from the scheme PDF and shown only after the reveal, because their model solution is a table, graph, construction or layout the text layer cannot carry: Q3(a) (the sum-to-product working), Q3(b) (method 4 continues on page 33), Q4(a)(ii), Q4(b) (the construction), Q5(a)(i) (the table), Q6(b) (the expected-value table), Q8(d)(i) (the table), Q8(d)(ii) (the graph) and Q9(a)(iii) (the confidence-interval methods continue on page 46).

The question booklet is LC003ALP200EV.pdf; its indexed scheme LC003ALP000EV.pdf is shared with Paper 1. Scheme page references are PDF positions (printed page number + 4 in this half of the scheme); question-paper PDF positions match the printed page numbers.

cards.questionText: Some time later a research institute surveyed a sample of 1000 full-time workers, randomly selected, and found that the mean annual income of the sample was €38 280. Test the hypothesis, at the 5 % level of significance, that the mean annual income of full-time workers has changed since the national data were published. State the null hypothesis and the alternative hypothesis. Give your conclusion in the context of the question.

The research institute surveyed 400 full-time farmers, randomly selected from all the full-time farmers in the country, and found that the mean income for the sample was €26 974 and the standard deviation was €5120. Assuming that annual farm income is normally distributed in this country, create a 95 % confidence interval for the mean income of full-time farmers.

It is known that data on farm size are not normally distributed. The research institute could take many large random samples of farm size and create a sampling distribution of the means of all these samples. Give one reason why they might do this.
The research institute also carried out a survey into the use of agricultural land. n farmers were surveyed. If the margin of error of the survey was 4·5 %, find the value of n.
